messages.content: 'Missed call de dena' English mein kya bolte hain?
Say: "Give me a missed call." People in India understand this. Elsewhere, you can say: "Ring me once, and I'll call you back."
Please tell what is wrong: "I am agree with you."
Correct form: "I agree with you." Why: "agree" is a verb, so we do not use "am" before it.
Aur "I am not agree" kaise bolun?
Say: "I do not agree." Why: the negative uses "do not" with the base verb.
College office mein poochna hai ki admission ki last date kya hai. Kaise?
Ask: "Excuse me, what is the last date for admission?" You can add: "Is there a form I should fill in?"
Please check: "I have went to the temple yesterday."
The correct sentence is: "I went to the temple yesterday."
Meeting aage badhwani hai. Colleague ko kaise bolun?
Say: "Could we postpone the meeting?" If you mean moving it earlier, say "move it earlier" instead.
"Jitna ho sake utna jaldi bhej do" ko English mein bolna hai.
It is: "Please send it as soon as possible." You may also say: "Please send it as quickly as you can."
Bachche ko aaj school se jaldi lena hai. Teacher ko kaise bataun?
Say: "I need to pick up my child early today. Is that all right?" You can add the time you will arrive if you know it.
"Mujhe ek minute do." Polite aur casual dono mein bolo.
Polite: "Could you give me a minute, please?" Casual: "Hold on a sec."
"Mujhe lift de do" polite aur casual mein kaise bolun?
Polite: "Could you give me a lift, please?" Casual: "Can you drop me on the way?"
Madad ke baad "Aapka bahut shukriya" ko formal aur casual mein kaise kahun?
Formal: "Thank you very much for your help. I really appreciate it." Casual: "Thanks a lot!"
"Is baar main fail nahi hounga." English?
It is: "I will not fail this time." You can also say: "I won't fail this time."
"Dukaan band ho chuki thi." English mein?
It is: "The shop had already closed."
"The shop was closed" bhi chalega?
Yes. "Was closed" tells us the state when we arrived. "Had already closed" shows it closed before we came.
Aur "The shop is closed"?
That is for now. Use it when you are looking at the closed shop at this moment.
"Tumne mujhe bataya kyun nahi?" Translate karo.
It is: "Why didn't you tell me?"
Boss se bolna hai "Mujhe aaj jaldi jaana hai." Kaise?
Say: "May I leave early today?" If you want to give a reason, add: "I have an appointment this afternoon."
Maine kaha "I will discuss about the project." Teacher ne roka. Kyun?
Because "discuss" already means "talk about", so "about" is not needed after it. Say: "I will discuss the project."
My little brother is very fond for sweets.

My little brother is very fond of sweets.
Why: The adjective "fond" is followed by "of", not "for".
Auto mein bolna hai "Mujhe yahin utaar dijiye." English?
Say: "Please drop me here."
Dost ne kaha "It happens once in a blue moon." Iska matlab?
It means it happens very rarely.
Which is right: 'He is my best friend since childhood' or 'He has been my best friend since childhood'?
The second one is right: "He has been my best friend since childhood." When something started in the past and is still true now, use the present perfect (has been) with "since".
Match haarne ke baad coach ko English mein kya bolun? Kuch acha sa.
You could say: "Thank you for training us, Coach. We lost today, but we learned a lot, and we'll work harder for the next match." It's honest, and it shows you respect the coach's effort.
